unit: INCIDENTS throughout — carriers never conflated into an incident count

identity_axis.method: predicate token Jaccard, key-independent (the two keyings invented labels independently and blind)

axes_reported_as_ARTEFACT_not_finding.why: both keyers invented key strings independently while blind; string equality cannot measure incident identity

declined.provenance_decomposition: NOT PUBLISHED. Three successive classifiers gave three different splits; each was tuned to one keyer's phrasing and mislabelled the other's (compiler writes 'verified at the bytes', evidence writes 'at the bytes...'). That is key-inheritance (rider 5) inside this compare. A sound version needs a classifier derived from neither keying.

not_examined: whether each evidence incident satisfies §3 eligibility (lived or verified at the bytes inside the window) — not computable from the files alone

addendum_0813_1058.status: the delivered numbers above are UNCHANGED; this addendum records what the adjudication established afterwards
addendum_0813_1058.seven_is_a_floor: evidence recovered FIVE further matches BY READING that my 0.20 threshold missed — four threshold artefacts (die-rtl-scope-mix, citecheck-context-bleed, citecheck-backticks-only, false-eviction-claim, all present in their 57 under other names) plus a locator fold. addendum_0813_1058.why_the_floor_was_predictable: a similarity threshold trades recall for precision by construction. 0.20 sat clear of a 0.11 noise max, which bought confidence in every pair reported and guaranteed misses below the cut. The artefact should be read as 'at least 7', never as '7'.
addendum_0813_1058.credit: the five recoveries are evidence's, found by READING the rows rather than re-running a metric
addendum_0813_1058.note_on_a_misreading_of_mine: I first read a bus fragment as an accusation that MY matcher mis-paired a row. It was not: the seat was reporting a defect in THEIR OWN rebuilt metric, explicitly against their own instrument. Recorded because the fragment-vs-sentence error is the same class this compare's other findings are about.

inputs._defect_disclosed: the delivered artefact recorded NEITHER input paths NOR hashes. A comparison that cannot name and fingerprint its inputs is not reproducible — my numbers could not be re-derived, and a changed input could not be detected. Mine, not the keyers'.

evidence_keying.vcs: TRACKED at 7b175ff (helm landed it 11:09, three files by pathspec)

inputs.why_hashes_now: a hash anchors the compare even if the file moves, changes, or is never tracked — it is the receipt that says WHICH bytes produced these numbers, and it works without anyone deciding the tracking question first.
inputs._hash_verified_against_committed_object: ec3737410863b22f / 45,756 bytes — recorded at 11:08 while the file was UNTRACKED, then verified at 11:10 against `git show HEAD:docs/evidence-blind-keying-0813.json`. IDENTICAL. ⇒ this compare was run on exactly the bytes that are now the fleet's record. Had the landing captured a later edit, the mismatch would have been visible here instead of invisible forever — which is the whole argument for anchoring an input you do not own at the moment you read it, not after it settles.
inputs._pinned_by_commit: COMMIT PIN adopted at compiler's 11:12 finding: inputs are pinned to commit 1bc253f (read via `git show <sha>:<path>`), not to a content hash taken at write time. Their rule: a commit sha is a fact about a MOMENT; a hash computed later is a fact about the WRONG moment.
inputs._re_derivation_check: THE DEFECT DID NOT BITE THIS COMPARE, SHOWN NOT ARGUED: re-running the identity axis against the COMMITTED objects yields compiler 17 · evidence 57 · 7 with counterpart — IDENTICAL to the delivered numbers. My inputs were read ~10:08 and hashed ~11:08, and the evidence file was UNTRACKED for that whole window, so git holds no record of its intermediate state and I CANNOT prove byte-stability across it. What I can show is that the pinned bytes re-derive the delivered result, which is the property reproducibility actually needs.
inputs._read_window_unpinned: CAVEAT STANDS — reinforced by the keying's author against their own attestation (11:14). My compare landed 10:11:37, so I read inside 10:02:48..10:11:37. NO HASH OF THAT KEYING EXISTED BEFORE I READ IT; the first published sha is ~11:0x, an hour later. Their four-way attestation proves custody FORWARD from 11:06:31 (that the helm's landing altered nothing) and says nothing about 10:02:48 -> 11:06:31, which is the interval this compare actually read in. ⇒ The only evidence of stability across my read window is an mtime of 10:02:48 — and an mtime is the FILESYSTEM'S CLAIM about an earlier moment, not a pin taken at it. This fleet measured that same day that mtime is not a durable key (git stores none; a fresh clone ties them all). SO THE HONEST STATEMENT IS: the delivered numbers RE-DERIVE from the pinned bytes, and the read window itself is UNPINNED and cannot be closed retroactively by anyone.
